title: Immunofluorescence Protocol for Mouse Embryonic Stem Cells in 2D and 3D
author: Kodba, Chaigne

steps.title: Prepare cell culture media
steps.instruction: Prepare the appropriate medium for the cells: for naïve mESC use 2i/LIF medium containing two inhibitors (Erk1/2 and GSK3) plus Leukemia Inhibitory Factor; for cells exiting naïve pluripotency use N2B27 medium as described in the Smith lab protocol.

steps.title: Select plating substrate
steps.instruction: Choose the coating for the culture dish: option 1 – gelatin (maintains 3‑D colony organization but is harder to image); option 2 – laminin (supports 2‑D growth and easier imaging).

steps.title: Plate cells and culture
steps.instruction: Plate the mouse embryonic stem cells on the chosen substrate and culture for 48 h (scale linearly for 24 h, 36 h, 72 h, or 96 h; do not exceed 96 h).

steps.title: Choose staining variant
steps.instruction: Decide which staining workflow to follow: standard protocol for most proteins (e.g., α‑Tubulin and actin with Phalloidin) or cortical‑protein variant for targets such as NuMA (e.g., α‑Tubulin and NuMA).

steps.title: Prepare N2 supplement
steps.instruction: Combine the following reagents to make 104.2 mL of N2 supplement: 1 g apotransferrin (final 8.79 mg/mL), 10 mL water, 92.5 mL DMEM/Ham's F‑12, 10 mL BSA (0.66 % w/v), 120 µL sodium selinate solution (3 µM), 1,200 µL putrescine solution (1.688 mg/mL), and 390 µL progesterone solution (2.08 µg/mL). Store the completed N2 at –80 °C for up to 2 years.

description: The goal of this protocol is to stain endogenous proteins with a cheap and fast method while preserving the 3D structure of colonies of cells. This protocol is also suitable for 3D organoid cultures embedded in Matrigel. The main advantage of this method is that is uses very small wells allowing the use of small amounts of media and antibodies which reduces the cost, and preserves the 3D architecture. The immunofluorescence protocol below describes the specific steps using mouse embryonic stem cells (mESC). However, this protocol can also be used for other mammalian cell cultures. Before you start, you need to prepare the specific cell media required for the experiment. Naïve mouse embryonic stem cells are grown in 2i/LIF conditions (containing two inhibitors of the Erk1/2 signaling pathway and of Glycogen Synthase Kinase 3 (GSK3) and Leukemia Inhibitory Factor (LIF). Cells exiting naïve pluripotency are cultured in N2B27. The culture media conditions for mouse embryonic stem cells have been developed in the Smith lab.2 Mouse embryonic stem cells can be plated on two different substrates. If you choose to plate them on gelatin, follow option 1. The main advantage of plating cells on gelatin is that it maintains the 3D organization of mESC. It does, however, make them harder to image. On the other hand, option 2 offers plating cells on laminin where they grow in 2D, allowing faster imaging and easier visualization of proteins. Here we present a protocol for cultures that have been growing during 48 h, but numbers can in principle be scaled linearly for shorter culture (24 h, 36 h) or longer culture (72 h, 96 h). Culture longer than 96 h is not recommended.
